pages.x: Macedon was a rough kingdom north of Greece until Philip II built a new army: pikemen with spears over five metres long in a dense block, the phalanx, and heavy cavalry. By 338 BC he had beaten Athens and Thebes and planned to invade Persia. In 336 he was murdered at his daughter's wedding.

His son Alexander, 22, crossed into Asia in 334 BC with about 40,000 men. He won at the river Granicus, nearly losing his life, and in 333 at Issus routed King Darius III, who fled and left his mother, wife and daughters in Alexander's camp.

Tyre, a Phoenician city on an island, refused to open its gates. Alexander built a causeway across 800 metres of sea and took it after seven months. Egypt then welcomed him as pharaoh, and on its coast he founded Alexandria.

In 331 BC Darius met him again near Gaugamela with a far bigger army and chariots with scythes on their wheels. Alexander led his cavalry into a gap in the Persian line, straight at Darius, who fled once more and was later killed by his own men. The Persian Empire was Alexander's.
pages.cap: The Alexander Mosaic from Pompeii, with Darius in his chariot

pages.x: At Persepolis, the great palace of the Persian kings, Alexander's men emptied the treasury. Then, after a drinking party, the palace was set on fire. Ancient writers disagree whether it was revenge for the burning of Athens or just drunkenness. Its ruins still stand.

pages.t: To the edge of the world
pages.x: He pushed on through Central Asia into India, where in 326 BC he beat King Porus and his war elephants at the river Hydaspes. But his men, eight years from home, refused to go further. On the way back many died crossing the Gedrosian desert.

In 323 BC, planning to conquer Arabia, Alexander fell ill after a banquet in Babylon and died at 32. Asked who should have his empire, he is said to have answered: the strongest. His generals fought over it for 40 years and split it into kingdoms.

In eleven years Alexander built an empire from Greece to India. It broke apart at once, but the Greek kingdoms that followed spread Greek language, cities and art across the Middle East for centuries, and mixed them with the cultures of Persia, Egypt and India.
pts: Conquered the Persian Empire in eleven years
Founded Alexandria and dozens of other cities
Spread Greek culture to the edge of India
